answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% with no buffer, switching or deferring adds delivery risk; adding a second source protects supply but does not meet the 18% spend cut this cycle. Negotiating renewal terms with the incumbent is the only single move that can pursue the mandated reduction while preserving continuity: prior renewals kept integration stable, renewal benchmarking recovered margin, and longer-term/volume commitments reduced unit cost without narrowing scope. I am verifying the two cost-lever memories before committing because the decision depends on whether price/terms concessions are realistically repeatable.
